findings.message: 117 AC-3 says the GitHub app now has "one state every consumer switches on", but only the Integrations suggestions were moved to it. The "Connect GitHub" suggestion still checks `myGitAccounts().configured`, which is `hasSecret` alone (server/read.ts:24), and so does the daily Connect nudge. When the stored value is incomplete, people are still offered and nudged to connect, and every attempt ends in the incomplete refusal. Fix: base connect-side readiness on the same check (`parseGitHubApp` through `appUsable`, run in the connect's system context so non-Admins get an answer too). Expose it as one flag that both the Connect suggestion and the nudge read, and add a test row for an incomplete app on /git-accounts.
findings.scenario: Admin stores `only-the-secret-00000000000000` → Integrations shows Incomplete, but Kasun on /git-accounts still gets the "Connect GitHub" chip and the nudge; Connect → "GitHub app incomplete" refusal

findings.message: `appUsable` keeps a successful answer per tenant for as long as `rotatedAt` doesn't change, so a check that can no longer run still reads as `ready`. The same outage (no key service, a different KMS key, a missing data key) shows `unchecked` if it starts before the first check and `ready` if it starts after a cached success. The status then reports a credential nobody can read as Configured. Fix: give the cached success a short lifetime, or drop it when any `useSecret` on github-oauth fails, so the status only says `ready` when the latest check worked. Add a table row: ready, then KMS removed, then expect unchecked.
findings.scenario: Status read once → ready (cached); operator unsets AMAX_KMS; status again → still `ready` / "Configured", while connect fails with "no key service is set"

findings.message: Each of the three Integrations suggestions calls `githubAppStatus` on its own. A failed check is dropped from the cache, so during an outage one render makes three separate audited credential reads. They can also answer differently (for example, Rotate hidden but Remove shown in the same render). Fix: read the state once per request and share it across the three `when` checks.
findings.scenario: KMS flaps during one render → first read fails (unchecked: only Remove), second succeeds (ready: Rotate) → the suggestions mix two states

findings.message: 118 moved the chip, the count, the pin's offer and the card to `needsOwner`. The Suggested-owner accept guard (and agent.ts:67, which gates on `open(p)` separately) still uses `hasNoOwner`. It relies on the asynchronous outbox `tidy` to withdraw the suggestion once the proposal is released. Fix: use `needsOwner` in the accept guard so the rule has one copy.
findings.scenario: Proposal released; before the outbox tick withdraws the suggestion, a PM accepts "Make X the owner" → an owner is set on a released proposal the screens show as Not recorded with no owner offer

findings.message: The test covers only the pure `githubMismatchForward`. Nothing drives `proxy()` itself, so moving the forward below the `isPublicPath` or `guarded` early return, or a matcher change, would go unnoticed. Add a case that calls `proxy` with a signed-out `/?error=redirect_uri_mismatch&state=…` request and asserts the redirect to the callback.
findings.scenario: Forward line moved after `if (!guarded || isPublicPath…) return NextResponse.next()` → /signin?error=redirect_uri_mismatch is no longer forwarded; the tests stay green

findings.message: The second assertion, `said === NO_KEY_SERVICE && !/key service/.test(String(words))`, can't fail for any row as written (every row's expected words either allow the key-service message or never produce it). It checks nothing. Drop it, or replace it with an exact expected message per row.
findings.scenario: problemOf returns NO_KEY_SERVICE for the 'anything else' row → the first assertion fails, but the second never adds anything
